memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Adam made love to his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, "God has granted me another child in place of Abel, since Cain killed him." - Gen 4:25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the darkness of this chapter - a murder, a wandering line, a song of vengeance - God gives a gift of grace. A new son, Seth, whose name sounds like "granted" or "appointed." Eve's words are full of quiet faith: "God has granted me another child in place of Abel." She sees this birth not as chance, but as God's gracious provision.

Grief still marks her words - she remembers Abel, remembers Cain's crime. Loss leaves its ache. But through her sorrow shines hope. God had not abandoned His purposes. Where sin took a son, grace granted another. And it is through Seth's line, not Cain's, that God's promise of a Saviour would one day come (Luke 3:38).

This is how God works throughout the whole Bible. Human sin does not defeat His plans; His grace always has the last word. When one door closes in loss, He is already opening another in mercy.

Perhaps you are living in the space between loss and hope right now. Take heart. The God who granted Seth to Eve is faithful still. He can bring new grace out of old grief, and He is quietly weaving even your story into His good and redemptive plan.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Can you see God's grace even in a season of loss?
- Where might God be granting new hope after grief?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Gracious God, thank You that Your mercy has the last word over sin and sorrow. Help me trust Your faithful hand to bring new grace out of my grief.
